title: The Wolf of Caerlum
premise: Noor Ashgrove has spent her life stealing memories to survive, trading other people's pasts for coin while keeping her own carefully blank. When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, she learns the court beneath Caerlum mountain has called in an old debt: her mother sold Noor's soul before she was born, and the debt is now due. To reclaim it, Noor must steal back the one memory she never took—her own first stolen moment—and carry it into the dark court as both key and ransom. She succeeds by giving up the memory forever, choosing a future built on belonging over the safety of forgetting.
about_author: Lena Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed. She writes fantasy about the things we inherit and the things we choose to forget, from a cottage full of unlabeled boxes.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Noor steals a widow's grief-memory in the market town of Dunhollow, trading it to a memory-broker for passage money. Her POV establishes her rules: never keep what you steal, never be remembered. But the widow's memory contains a glimpse of Caerlum's gates—and Noor feels an ache she can't name. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Wards Like Broken Glass
chapters.summary: The border wards shatter at moonrise and every star goes out at once. From a smuggler's ridge, Noor watches refugees flood the passes and realizes only someone with her knowledge of hidden roads could have slipped through unnoticed—someone like her. A dying ward-keeper grabs her wrist and whispers her true surname: Ashgrove of Caerlum. Beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: What the Broker Wouldn't Buy
chapters.summary: Noor confronts her old broker, Sef, demanding records of her childhood trades. He reveals her mother sold not memories but Noor's soul itself, sealed under Caerlum when she was an infant. POV shifts briefly to Sef, showing his guilt. Noor flees with a torn ledger page. Beat: the ground of her identity gives way.

chapters.title: Roads Only Thieves Remember
chapters.summary: Noor guides a small refugee column—including the widow from chapter one—through forgotten smuggler paths as the starless dark deepens. Along the way she discovers her stolen memories are unraveling; the ones she sold are dissolving everywhere, as if Caerlum is calling them home. Beat: reluctant tenderness toward people she meant to abandon.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Noor reaches Caerlum's sunken gate and barges into the Undercourt, where the pale Queen of Quiet Hours keeps souls in jars of starlight—the missing stars. The Queen shows Noor the contract bearing her mother's signature. Noor offers a trade: a rare memory for her soul. The Queen names the price. Beat: dread braided with defiance.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Milk Teeth
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, half in the Queen's memory-vaults: young Noor's mother, desperate and pregnant, bargaining away her unborn child's soul to save the father from Undercourt justice. Present-day Noor realizes her whole life of theft was shaped by that hollow where her soul should sit. Beat: grief for a mother she'd only resented.

chapters.title: Everything I Ever Sold
chapters.summary: Noor tracks down buyers of her old stolen memories across the starless countryside, buying or begging them back—but each recovered memory crumbles to ash at Caerlum's threshold. The widow, following her, offers her most precious memory freely. Noor refuses to take it. Beat: learning that some things must be given, not taken.

chapters.title: The First Stolen Moment
chapters.summary: Sef arrives with the ledger's missing page: Noor's very first theft, at age four—she stole a moment of her mother singing. That memory is the contract's seal, held in the Queen's vault. Noor infiltrates the vault through the mountain's drowned mines, nearly drowning, and takes it back. Beat: courage born of desperation.

chapters.title: Ransom of One Small Song
chapters.summary: Climax. In the Undercourt, Noor demands her soul. The Queen agrees—but the exchange requires the memory to pass permanently into the vault, sung aloud until it fades. Noor sings her mother's lullaby as her soul returns and the stars stream back into the sky through the mountain's crown. Beat: sacrifice transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: Ashgrove, Rooted
chapters.summary: Noor wakes on the mountainside among the refugees, soul intact but the lullaby gone—she remembers that she loved it, not how it went. The widow hums a fragment she somehow kept, and the settlement they've begun building takes the name Ashgrove. Noor stays, visible at last. Beat: quiet joy; belonging chosen, not stolen.
